source.title: Grokking as a Phase Transition between Competing Basins: a Singular Learning Theory Approach
source.authors: B. Cullen; Sergio Estan-Ruiz; Riya Danait; Jiayi Li

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; its title differs from the title in the ID metadata.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures LLC trajectories alongside training and validation performance in a modular-addition grokking experiment. This is a different measure and setting from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The main experiment reports a qualitative training/validation transition and LLC trajectory. The paper also describes width-dependent final LLC and learning-rate-dependent grokking severity, but those findings do not directly measure a listed version. Cited prior-work findings are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests an LLC account of modular-addition grokking, but none of V1–V8. LLC and unscaled Hessian trace do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness; width-dependent LLC and eventual generalization do not establish V2's decreasing test error beyond interpolation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate as an interpretation: the authors propose competing memorizing and generalizing basins with different LLCs and report trajectories consistent with that picture. Their theory characterizes Bayesian basin preference rather than deriving the SGD transition; extending the results beyond simplified quadratic models remains open.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses quadratic networks on modular addition and tracks LLC and validation behavior; it does not test the listed interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that grokking severity decreases as learning rate increases; LLC estimates vary substantially with SGLD localization strength and learning rate, so the authors keep sampler hyperparameters fixed for comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 100 seeds, LLC peaks and then declines around the delayed validation-accuracy improvement while training accuracy remains saturated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-data LLC trajectories track delayed generalization in quadratic networks on modular addition.

fits_no_version.finding: After training and validation accuracies saturate, LLC continues decreasing while Hessian trace increases (Section 6.2, Figure 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unscaled Hessian trace and LLC can diverge without changing classifier accuracy after grokking.

fits_no_version.finding: Final LLC increases with width even though all tested widths eventually generalize (Section 6.1, Figure 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger final LLC across network widths can coexist with successful modular-addition generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger learning rates are associated with lower grokking severity and smaller peak LLC values (Appendices H.3–H.4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning rate affects the duration of delayed generalization and peak estimated LLC in the tested quadratic networks.

record.problems: The empirical evidence is from simplified quadratic networks on modular addition. The paper says its Bayesian asymptotic characterization does not directly analyze SGD dynamics; LLC estimation is sensitive to sampler hyperparameters, and absolute LLC values are interpreted up to an estimator-dependent scale.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were extracted as rows: width-dependent final LLC does not report a corresponding test-error comparison, and learning-rate-dependent grokking severity is reported in Figure 9 without numerical values in the text.

untested.parts: Matched random-label and natural-label fitting and held-out performance.
Whether test error keeps decreasing as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under different tuning recipes.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes and regularization recipes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness versus generalization gaps, including rankings against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Neither memorization during grokking nor eventual generalization alone tests V1 or V8. The post-generalization Hessian-trace increase does not challenge V7 because the study does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness. Figures are represented by captions and prose in the supplied text, so exact plotted values cannot be checked.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural labels.
Test-error behavior as width passes the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: two-layer quadratic network
rows.operation_detail: Tracked LLC, training loss, and validation loss during training.
rows.measure: LLC trajectory alongside training and validation loss
rows.value: LLC rises to a peak and then declines; validation performance remains poor after training loss rapidly collapses, then validation accuracy increases sharply.
rows.uncertainty: ±1 standard deviation shaded regions; numeric LLC and accuracy values not stated in text.
rows.note: Results are aggregated over 100 random seeds. This is a modular-addition grokking setting, not one of the listed claim versions.
rows.check: The trajectory is accurately described, but it cannot determine any listed version's effect. The measure also includes training and validation accuracies, not only losses. The reported conditions match Figure 2.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
